## TL;DR

Compared every `repoos` command's `--help` output and the common error messages
against `user-docs/cli.md`, found nine commands documented nowhere, two help
lines that omitted documented flags, and three error surfaces that answered
with server jargon or raw HTML instead of plain English. Fixed all of it, plus
added a table-driven test that fails CI the next time a `--help` command is
missing from the docs. The QA narrative lives in
`docs/qa/2026-11-cli-help-qa.md`.

## Work and rationale

**Docs coverage (the biggest gap).** `repoos rm`, `watch`, `summary`,
`review followup`, `allowlist`, `certify`, `migrate`, `checks
timings`/`checks slots`, and `release email` all appeared in `repoos --help`
but had no mention in `user-docs/cli.md` — a user reading the manual could not
discover them. I added each one in the style of its neighbours: `###` sections
for standalone commands (`rm`, `certify`, `migrate`, `release email`,
`checks timings/slots`) and rows in the Control-plane table for the
server-backed ones (`summary`, `review followup`, `watch`, `allowlist`). I
read each command's implementation before writing its description so the docs
state real behaviour (e.g. `rm` refuses without `--yes`; `release email`
renders without sending; `allowlist` pause/resume propagates to group members).

**Help lines that omitted documented flags.** `repoos check --help` did not
list `--fix` or `--step <name>`, although the docs document both and
`parseCheckArgs` accepts them — the exact drift the docs warn about for
`repoos new`'s generated help, but in the hand-maintained table. `repoos
doctor --help` omitted `--model <id>` for the opt-in `--probe` run. Both fixed
in `src/cli/help.ts`; the existing pinned-string test in
`cli-help-doctor.test.ts` was updated to the docs-matching value.

**Plain-English errors.** Three fixes, each chosen because a real invocation
showed the confusion:

- `repoos api GET /api/<typo>` printed `"status": 200` and dumped the entire
  single-page-app shell as an HTML "error" string, exiting 0 — it looked like
  success. `RepoOsApi.request` now detects an HTML body and returns a one-line
  message ("…is not a RepoOS API route. Check the path for typos…") plus an
  `htmlResponse` marker; `repoos api` prints it to stderr and exits 1, and
  every other CLI consumer gets the same short message through `requestOk`.
- `repoos config set bogus.key 1` failed with the server's generic
  `No valid fields to update`, which named neither the key nor the fix. The
  CLI rewrites exactly that reply into
  `Unknown setting "bogus.key" — RepoOS has no config field with that name…`
  pointing at Settings and `repoos config get`. The rewrite is deliberately
  CLI-side and message-specific, so the server contract and the UI are
  untouched.
- Every unknown project environment answered the bare `Unknown project
  environment`. The route now names the environment and points at the Secrets
  page, via a small exported `unknownEnvironmentError()` helper reused by all
  four 404 sites (secrets list/add/replace/delete, the editor route, and the
  bindings PUT path).

**Drift guard.** A new `cli-help-docs-coverage.test.ts` exports the help
table's `GROUPS` and asserts every command (including two-word entries like
`checks timings` and sub-commands like `review followup`) is documented in
`user-docs/cli.md`, with a negative-lookahead regex so `repoos new` cannot be
satisfied by the `repoos new-doc` heading. It also pins the fixed flag pairs
and unit-tests the new error helpers.

## Approaches tried

- I first probed the live CLI against the real running server for error
  reproduction — cheap and honest, using only nonexistent ids, invalid values,
  and GET requests.
- For the HTML-response fix I considered changing the server's SPA catch-all
  to 404 unknown `/api/` paths, which would fix every client at once — but it
  risks breaking in-app fetches that rely on the current fallback and is a
  wider blast radius than a QA task should take. Detecting the HTML body in
  the CLI client achieves the same user outcome locally.
- The docs-coverage test could have compared flag-by-flag against the docs
  markdown; that would be brittle against prose rewording, so I scoped it to
  command-level coverage plus explicit pins for the flags that actually
  drifted.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Editor/shell visibility mismatch.** Mid-session my file edits briefly
  seemed to vanish; investigation showed my shell's working directory was the
  main checkout, so shell probes (and one `sed -i`) were reading and writing
  the wrong tree. I reverted the main checkout's accidental modification
  immediately (`git checkout -- src/server/routes/project-environments.ts`,
  confirmed clean) and redid everything with absolute worktree paths. No
  unreverted changes remain in the main checkout.
- **A stray `git stash pop`** (of a pre-existing unnamed stash, not mine)
  conflicted two other tasks' `work/` files; I resolved it with
  `git reset --hard HEAD` on the clean worktree, leaving the stash itself
  untouched, and stopped using stash entirely.
- **The docs build broke on my own edit.** A multi-line code span in the new
  `certify` section (`\`--binary\n<path>\``) made VitePress's Vue compiler
  fail with "Element is missing end tag" — surfaced indirectly as a confusing
  llms-enrich ENOENT because the enrich plugin's `closeBundle` runs over a
  build the parse failure aborted. I bisected each new section with isolated
  builds to find it and put `--binary <path>` on one line. Worth noting for
  future docs work: VitePress treats a wrapped code span as fatal.

## Key learnings

**Follow-up from the first handoff (UI verification).** The review shot of the
`/cli` docs page failed ui verification with horizontal overflow at both
viewport widths (body scrollWidth 1594 > 1024px, 1282 > 375px). Reproducing it
locally showed the overflow was pre-existing, not from this pass's additions —
the identical numbers appear with the original cli.md. Two structural causes:
the `repoos story` example's fenced code block was never closed (its fence
swallowed the whole schedule section until a stray closing fence after the
schedules subcommand table — 45 fence markers, an odd count), and a
4-space-indented `repoos update 0612 --shots …` line rendered as a bare
`<pre>` that gets no `overflow-x` container in the VitePress theme, so its
1258px `<code>` pushed the body wide. Fixed both (rebalanced the fences,
converted the line to a fenced block) and re-measured: no overflow at 1024px
or 375px, and no non-scrollable element past the viewport. The lesson general
to docs edits here: an unbalanced fence in one section silently re-renders
several sections as code, and only a rendered-page check catches it —
`repoos check` does, once a shot names the page.



- Hand-maintained help tables drift exactly the way generated ones can't; the
  fix is not a one-off edit but a test that walks the table against the docs.
- Error messages that come from a server ("No valid fields to update") reach
  users through many CLI commands; rewriting the message at the CLI boundary,
  keyed on the exact server string, keeps the server contract stable while
  fixing the human experience — and is unit-testable without a server.
- The worktree/main-checkout boundary is the sharpest edge in this repo:
  always verify `pwd` and use absolute paths for every tool, because a
  relative `sed` against the wrong checkout is indistinguishable from success
  until something breaks.
